items.t: Elon Musk and Anthropic make promises to give the public a piece of the AI pie
items.d: Elon Musk and officials at AI giant Anthropic are pledging to give coveted shares in their companies to the general public as concerns about AI’s economic and societal impact continue to pile up.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Elon Musk and Anthropic make promises to give the public a piece of the AI pie The promises come as the public has broadly soured on AI and concerns about its economic impact grow. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Elon Musk is awarded the National Medal of Science during the Golden Age of American Innovation Summit in Washington on Oct. 8. Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 19, 2026, 10:39 AM EDT By Rob Wile Elon Musk and officials at AI giant Anthropic are pledging to give coveted shares in their companies to the general public as concerns about AI’s economic and societal impact continue to pile up . “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America,” Musk posted on X on Monday. “This will be the first of many.” One SpaceX share is currently valued at about $150. With approximately 72 million children under the age of 18 in the U.S., Musk’s donation would currently be worth about $10.8 billion — less than 2% of his current net worth. He provided no additional information. Musk could not be reached for additional comment. His statement comes one day after officials at Anthropic said the company would commit 5% of company shares to a “public benefit fund” in order to address “labor market impacts” of AI. In a statement, Anthropic officials said the fund could make charitable donations or direct money to “specific populations,” emphasizing the fund’s “versatility.” “Given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed,” they said. Anthropic has been preparing for an initial public offering — releasing its stock for trading on public markets — that analysts say would value the company at more than $1 trillion. The company has long championed employees’ charitable giving by promising to match their donations. Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic. items.t: Musk pledges to give ‘every kid in America’ one of his SpaceX shares
items.d: Musk's post came just a few hours after Anthropic promised to put 5% of its shares into a new "public benefit fund," which it intends to use to make "large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations" after its upcoming IPO.
items.fullText: Elon Musk claims he will give one of his SpaceX shares to “every kid in America” in 2027, which would result in a gift worth more than $10 billion based on the current $146 share price of his combination spaceflight and AI company. That’s roughly 1% of his $1 trillion net worth. It’s not clear how Musk plans to do this, though he said in a separate post that he wants to give the shares “directly to the public,” and that this will be the “first of many” shares he’ll donate. President Donald Trump, who Musk spent around $300 million to help elect, has set up bank accounts for children through the Treasury, called Trump Accounts, that can accept stock donations from wealthy donors. Musk did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Musk’s post came just a few hours after Anthropic promised to put 5% of its shares into a new “public benefit fund,” which it intends to use to make “large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations” after its upcoming IPO. On Sunday afternoon, Musk replied directly to Anthropic’s post on X about its new fund, suggesting the company should give “directly to the public” instead. “This is what I will be doing,” he wrote in another reply four hours later. Then, overnight, he announced his plans to donate SpaceX stock. There are currently more than 70 million children under the age of 18 in the United States, according to the Federal Interagency Forum on Child and Family Statistics . Musk owns around 849 million Class A common shares of SpaceX and more than 5.5 billion Class B supervoting shares. He stands to earn many more. Musk’s philanthropic giving to date has been almost exclusively done through his Musk Foundation. items.t: Elon Musk shows off ‘flying’ Tesla Roadster after years of delays
items.d: Elon Musk showed off the new Tesla Roadster prototype Thursday that can briefly launch itself into the air using rocket-inspired thrusters.
items.fullText: Tech News Elon Musk shows off ‘flying’ Tesla Roadster after years of delays The electric sports car performed aerial stunts using thrusters developed with SpaceX, but it’s still years from production, and its flying features aren’t approved for public roads. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Tesla unveils its next generation 'flying' Roadster 03:33 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 16, 2026, 11:58 AM EDT By Chris Perez Elon Musk showed off a new vehicle prototype Thursday that can briefly launch itself into the air using rocket-inspired thrusters. The Tesla Roadster made its debut eight years after it was first announced. The company has yet to announce a price or release date, though the Tesla and SpaceX CEO said production would not begin until 2028. In a stunt-filled demonstration at a SpaceX testing facility in Texas, Musk told the live audience that what they were about to see “was not AI or SI.” The vehicle, a collaboration between Tesla and SpaceX, then slowly drove up a curved ramp shaped like half of a roller coaster loop before accelerating and launching itself off the ramp, hurdling over five other Tesla vehicles and bringing itself to a soft landing in a cloud of condensation using cold-gas thrusters. “Well, it worked!” Musk said after the stunt, adding that “it’s not necessarily a safety-optimized car.” Tesla Tesla says a fan-based suction system creates downforce to hold the vehicle against the road’s surface, while self-refilling cold-gas thrusters power its airborne maneuvers.
